\subsubsection{As the Potentiostat Control Amplifier (A1)}\label{sss:ampab-ctrl}

As A1 the amplifier drives the counter electrode and closes its loop on the reference
electrode, holding that electrode at the commanded potential. The commanded potential is
swept over the full \SIrange{0}{2.5}{\volt} supply range.

The bench is Figure~\ref{fig:tb-celldrive}: a Randles cell with
$R_{\mathrm{CE}} = \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}$, $R_u = \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}$,
$R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$ and $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{1}{\micro\farad}$ ---
the only electrode model simulated --- and the working electrode held at
\SI{1.25}{\volt}. No load current is injected: the cell current follows from the sweep
against the cell impedance, and the regulation figures at \SI{\pm 10}{\micro\ampere} are
read off the sweep where the cell current crosses those values. Temperature is split as
for the device tables, \SI{37}{\celsius} at the typical point and \SI{25}{\celsius} at
the four skew corners.
